walkthroughs.body_html:
MZ twins share 100% of genes; DZ share ~50%.

If a trait is more concordant in MZ than DZ, genetics matters.

Kendler et al. (2006): heritability of major depression ≈ 38%.

Limits: shared environments inflate heritability estimates; rare genetic disorders are missed.

Environment switches genes on/off via methylation.

Weaver et al. (2004): poorly licked rat pups developed methylated glucocorticoid receptor genes, growing into anxious adults.

Some marks pass to the next generation — challenging strict gene-only determinism.

The brain rewires in response to experience.

Maguire et al. (2000): London taxi drivers showed enlarged posterior hippocampi after years memorising 'The Knowledge'.

Draganski et al. (2004): three months of juggling thickened gray matter in V5 (motion area).
